Program: Intergenerational Connections – Parkland at the Lakes
Description: Life enrichment staff at Parkland at the Lakes coordinate regular visits and co-programmed sessions with nearby licensed child care centres and preschools. Residents volunteer as program helpers—reading with children, assisting with crafts and music, and sharing skills—while child care partners use Parkland’s common rooms for group time, creating shared programming that supports early learning and increases social engagement for older adults.

Program: Kjipuktuk (Halifax) Community Land Trust
Description: A resident-led initiative creating a community land trust in Halifax to acquire land and steward permanently affordable homes. Description: Open Arms developed a small village of micro‑shelters (tiny homes) on community land in Kentville to provide heated, lockable cabins and shared facilities as a bridge to permanent housing. By engaging Dal’s diaspora—alumni living across Canada and abroad—the platform maintains a living database of mentors and hosts ongoing virtual meetups and programs that highlight career paths in Nova Scotia and support returning or investing back in the province.
Solution: Alumni & Diaspora Engagement Network: Build and maintain a community-managed database and regular programming for alumni and diaspora to share remote mentoring, investment, seasonal work, and returning opportunities—turning outward migration into a resource rather than a loss.

Program: Ten Thousand Coffees (Nova Scotia Community College - NSCC Connects)
Organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) Alumni Relations
Description: NSCC’s mentoring community on Ten Thousand Coffees connects students and recent graduates with NSCC alumni across industries for virtual coffee chats, career conversations, and project-based guidance. This alumni database and ongoing programming draw in NSCC’s diaspora—graduates working outside Nova Scotia—to mentor remotely, flag seasonal and full-time opportunities, and help peers navigate pathways to return or contribute to local enterprises.
Solution: Alumni & Diaspora Engagement Network: Build and maintain a community-managed database and regular programming for alumni and diaspora to share remote mentoring, investment, seasonal work, and returning opportunities—turning outward migration into a resource rather than a loss.

Program: Options and Opportunities (O2) Program
Description: O2 is a high school program that embeds career development into the curriculum through individualized career planning, co-op education, and community-based learning. Delivered in partnership with local employers and community organizations, it provides students with job-shadow days, workplace experiences, and exposure to local role models across trades, technology, health, arts, and community services, making visible the many pathways to fulfilling careers in Nova Scotia.
Solution: Visible Pathways in Schools and Youth Programs: Partner schools, community centres and trade boards to integrate local career mapping into curricula and extracurriculars, run job-shadow days and invite local role models to show students practical routes to fulfilling local careers.
